data.summary: Attention and choice dominate this week. Six books surfaced; three fit the shelf's lanes without overlapping what we already cover, and one is already on the shelf.

candidates.title: The Courage to Be Disliked
candidates.author: Ichiro Kishimi & Fumitake Koga
candidates.why: Dialogue between a philosopher and a young man. Each exchange is a self-contained reel with two voices.
hooks: You're not shy. You've decided it's safer not to try.
Other people's opinions are their task, not yours.
candidates.risk: Long dialogue; needs a two-voice script template.

candidates.title: Thinking in Bets
candidates.author: Annie Duke
candidates.why: Judging decisions by outcomes is a mistake everyone makes. Pairs naturally with Kahneman.
hooks: A bad outcome doesn't mean it was a bad decision.
You're 'resulting' and you don't know it.

candidates.title: The Scout Mindset
candidates.author: Julia Galef
candidates.why: Why some people see clearly and others defend. Very on-brand for 'the quiet part'.
hooks: Being right feels good. Seeing clearly feels better.
You argue like a soldier. Try thinking like a scout.

candidates.title: Range
candidates.author: David Epstein
candidates.why: Generalists in a specialist world. Good counter-narrative to the 10,000-hour rule.
hooks: The 10,000-hour rule only works in tidy worlds.
Late starters aren't behind. They're sampling.

candidates.title: How to Do Nothing
candidates.author: Jenny Odell
candidates.why: Attention as something to protect. Calm tone matches the night look.
hooks: Doing nothing is harder than it looks.
Your attention is the thing they're selling.
candidates.risk: Political chapters; stay on the attention material.

candidates.title: Stolen Focus
candidates.author: Johann Hari
candidates.why: Big audience, strong hooks on attention and phones.
hooks: You didn't lose your focus. It was taken.
candidates.risk: Several claims are contested; most would need a MIXED stamp.

data.request: Books about regret that aren't self-help.
data.summary: Two strong options. Both are research-led and avoid the advice-list format, and both have short chapters that map to single reels.

candidates.title: The Power of Regret
candidates.author: Daniel H. Pink
candidates.why: Built on a large regret survey; four regret types make a natural series.
hooks: Most regrets are about what you didn't do.
Regret is information, not a verdict.

candidates.title: Being Mortal
candidates.author: Atul Gawande
candidates.why: A surgeon on what matters at the end. Handle with care; the tone guide applies.
hooks: The question isn't how long. It's how well.
Ask what a good day looks like.
candidates.risk: Sensitive subject; needs the tone guide before any script.

data.summary: Quick run on money and motivation. One overlap with the shelf, one hidden gem worth a look.

candidates.title: Four Thousand Weeks
candidates.author: Oliver Burkeman
candidates.why: Already on the shelf. Listed because it scored highest on fit.
hooks: You'll never get it all done.

candidates.title: The Molecule of More
candidates.author: Daniel Z. Lieberman & Michael E. Long
candidates.why: Dopamine and wanting; strong visual metaphors.
hooks: Wanting and having use different chemistry.
The chase feels better than the catch.
candidates.risk: Pop neuroscience; check every claim against primary studies.

data.summary: Calm, evidence-led content is saving well, while hustle-framed productivity is losing shares. Money anxiety is rising; Housel and Burkeman are the right books to lean on this week.

formats.name: Lit-line reel
formats.why: One line in full ink against a ghost page holds attention without music.
formats.howWeUseIt: Default for hooks and closers. One lit line per frame.

formats.name: Paper carousel
formats.why: Slow, swipeable explainers are saving more than reels this month.
formats.howWeUseIt: Inside pages on paper, cover and close at night.

hooks.example: Everyone says twenty-one days. The study says sixty-six.
You're not tired of deciding. You're answering easier questions.

hashtags.note: Keep to five. Swap one rotating tag each week.

audio.howToUse: Under voiceover at about −28 LUFS. Fade out before the last line.

audio.name: Room tone and vinyl
audio.howToUse: Use on paper carousels. No melody.

data.headline: The systems line carried the week. The money post found a quieter audience.
data.note: sends > views. keep the stamp visible.

wins.why: AH-01 did 31k views and 1,240 sends. The hook is the book's best-known line, but the staircase visual gave it a second read. Sends were well above views-weighted average, which is the signal we care about.

patterns.pattern: Supported claims got twice the sends.
patterns.evidence: Supported claims averaged roughly twice the sends of philosophy posts. The evidence stamp on screen seems to give people permission to share.

misses.why: EN-02 underperformed. The line is familiar, and the reel spent four seconds on the source before the hook landed. Move the source chip after the first beat.

nextActions.action: Ship TFS-01 after the two QA fixes, then EN-04. Hold FTW-05 until Thursday so the two philosophy posts don't run back to back.

data.summary: A quiet week: two reels, both above the median.

wins.why: TFS-05 held attention to the end.
